title: Summit and Provision
premise: Yara Dunmore, a railroad engineer drifting between closed mountain lines, is hired to survey a route through the Karst Range before the winter snows and before the mining company's concession permits expire. In a tide-revealed cave, she finds not treasure but evidence that the company's founder falsified surveys and buried a village's water rights decades ago. Pursued by the company's fixer and joined by a ragtag crew of track-walkers, a disgraced surveyor, and an old guide who once worked those same lines, Yara must carry the proof across the range ahead of the snows. She reaches the county seat on the final day of the permits, files the documents under a forgotten homestead clause, and chooses at last to stop moving—keeping the found family she built on the way.
about_author: Elodie Winterbourne is the pen name of a former railway archivist who spent years cataloguing abandoned mountain lines and the communities they left behind. She writes adventure stories about people who find their place in the most unreachable corners of the map.

chapters.title: The Map of Closed Lines
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Drifting from job to job along shuttered rail spurs, Yara takes a survey contract through the Karst Range with a hard deadline: the concession permits expire when the snows come. We learn stopping has always cost her more than moving. Emotional beat: restless self-protection masking loneliness.

chapters.title: What the Tide Gave Back
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. At a coastal staging town, an extreme low tide exposes a sea cave locals call the Tollhouse, said to charge admission in stories. Inside she finds a rusted strongbox of old survey plates bearing the mining company's seal—and signs someone else has been there recently. Beat: curiosity overriding caution.

chapters.title: A Crew of Strays
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. To cross the range she hires what the townsfolk mockingly call the strays: track-walker brothers Fen and Odo, disgraced surveyor Maren Cole, and taciturn old guide Bram Halloway, who goes quiet at the cave's name. Beat: wary first bonds forming over shared meals and shared damage.

chapters.title: The Fixer Arrives
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Company fixer Silas Vane reaches the staging town, asking after a woman who took papers from the Tollhouse. Maren recognizes his methods from the scandal that ended her career and says nothing—but realizes Yara is carrying something dangerous. Beat: dread entering the story.

chapters.title: First Ascent
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. The crew begins the climb, running survey lines through fog and scree. Yara teaches Odo to read grades and discovers Bram knows the abandoned tunnels better than any living man should. Beat: competence as intimacy; the team starts to fit together.

chapters.title: The Village That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Crossing a dry valley, Bram finally speaks: the maps show no settlement because the company erased one. Lowden Hollow lost its water rights when its survey was buried—the same plates Yara found. Beat: grief surfacing; the journey gains a moral weight.

chapters.title: Vane's Offer
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Vane intercepts them at a waystation with a generous buyout and a veiled threat about Yara's own past—a bridge failure she was blamed for. He gives her three days to decide. Beat: temptation and shame; Yara nearly takes the money.

chapters.title: The Bridge She Didn't Burn
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Maren digs into the old bridge incident and finds the report was doctored too—by the same hand that buried Lowden Hollow's survey. She shows Yara the pattern. Beat: vindication turning to resolve; Yara stops running from her past and aims it forward.

chapters.title: Snowline
chapters.summary: Fen's POV. The weather turns early. A rockslide takes their supply sled, forcing brutal rationing. Fen, the younger brother, keeps Odo moving through the whiteout by inventing games. Beat: hardship forging loyalty; first real taste of the mountain's indifference.

chapters.title: The Tunnel Under the Pass
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Off-map, Bram leads them into a sealed company tunnel he helped build as a young man. Inside are the original bore records—proof the water diversion was deliberate. Vane's men are close behind. Beat: awe and claustrophobia; the evidence now undeniable.

chapters.title: Ambush at the Switchback
chapters.summary: Odo's POV. Vane's hired men attack on a narrow switchback. The strays fight not like soldiers but like people protecting each other; Odo takes a bad fall saving the document case. Beat: fear and courage; the stakes turn physical and personal.

chapters.title: The Long Camp
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Stormbound in a wrecked caboose, the crew tends Odo's leg and tells the stories they've each been carrying. Yara admits she kept moving so no one could get close enough to leave. Beat: the emotional heart—found family named aloud.

chapters.title: What Vane Wants
chapters.summary: Silas Vane's POV. Alone in his camp, Vane reveals he isn't merely a fixer: his father signed the false survey, and burying it again is his inheritance. He believes some truths cost more than they're worth. Beat: antagonist humanized without excused.

chapters.title: The Tollhouse Revisited
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. A second tide window lets them return to the cave, where they discover the recent intruder was a Lowden Hollow descendant who died trying to carry the proof out. They take up his unfinished errand. Beat: solemnity; the mission becomes a debt owed to the dead.

chapters.title: Race Above the Clouds
chapters.summary: Fen's POV. With the storm closing the high pass behind them, the crew pushes a handcar along a derelict ridge line, Vane's party paralleling below. It becomes a race measured in hours of daylight. Beat: exhilaration; pure adventure momentum.

chapters.title: Betrayal on the Trestle
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. One of Vane's men, embedded since the staging town, sabotages the trestle crossing. Maren catches him, but the delay costs them their lead and nearly costs Odo his life. Beat: shock and anger; trust tested and repaired by action.

chapters.title: Whiteout Descent
chapters.summary: Bram's POV. Off every map, Bram navigates the descent by memory and instinct through total whiteout, guided by sounds of water he hasn't heard in fifty years. Beat: quiet heroism; the old man's redemption run.

chapters.title: The Last Day of the Permits
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. They reach the county seat as the permit clock runs out—but the recorder's office is locked for a company function, and Vane stands on the steps with a sheriff's warrant naming Yara a thief. Beat: everything converging; despair before the final move.

chapters.title: Admission Paid
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. Yara invokes the Tollhouse legend itself: the cave's original claim predates the concession, and its admission clause grants public right-of-way to anyone who 'pays the toll'—which she has, in blood and miles. The crowd of rail families backs her. Beat: clever triumph; justice outside the law, inside the letter of an older one.

chapters.title: Vane's Choice
chapters.summary: Silas Vane's POV. Confronted with his father's signature and the assembled descendants of Lowden Hollow, Vane must choose: destroy the last plate or let it stand. He sets it down and walks into the snow. Beat: tragic release; the antagonist defeated by truth, not force.

chapters.title: Water for Lowden Hollow
chapters.summary: Maren's POV. Weeks later, the restored survey reopens the water rights and the spur line with them. The strays are offered jobs rebuilding it—all of them, together. Beat: warmth and belonging earned; the family formalized in work.

chapters.title: Where She Stops
chapters.summary: Yara's POV. On the completed line's first run, Yara passes the Tollhouse cave at low tide and doesn't look away this time. She signs the station ledger with a local address—the first she's written down in years. Beat: resolution; the woman who kept moving finally stays.
